explanation: The response recognizes only the broad topic of five-component HENA nanoparticles under heating. It does not reconstruct the target hypothesis that nominal high-entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion fail in sub-10 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles above roughly 673 K because surface-energy differences drive Au and Cu outward, followed by melting or evaporation and morphology and size changes. The reference to traditional alloying concepts is undeveloped and does not state the relevant prior theoretical expectation of entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion. A useful falsification experiment would require controlled in situ vacuum heating with temperature-resolved STEM-EDS and atomistic diffusivity measurements, testing whether Au/Cu surface enrichment, particle reshaping, loss of 2–4 nm particles, and size reduction occur. The supplied citation is scientifically irrelevant.
